Use PR11.instructions.md file for changes to the css
Using overflow-x: hidden on the body can mask underlying layout issues and may cause accessibility problems by hiding content from users who need to scroll horizontally (e.g., with screen magnification). It's better to identify and fix the element causing the overflow rather than hiding it globally. A common cause is an element with a width greater than 100vw or a large negative margin.
he overflow-x: hidden; property is also being added to the body element in this pull request, which is the correct approach. Applying it to the html element as well is redundant and can sometimes cause unintended side effects with the page's scrollbar, such as hiding it completely. It's recommended to only have this property on the body element.
